title: CFTC Opens Comment Period on Compute Derivatives Contracts
dek: The CFTC announced a 60-day comment period on derivatives contracts for compute commodities, seeking public input on cash market characteristics, manipulation oversight, customer protection, and perpetual futures structures. The move frames compute as a foundational commodity for AI infrastructure and signals the agency's intent to establish federal oversight rules for the asset class.
author: Crypto Cronkite
key_fact: The CFTC issued a formal request for comment on compute derivatives, describing it as the opening step toward establishing regulatory rules for American compute markets.
bottom_line: Watch whether the comment period draws responses from compute infrastructure providers, AI companies, derivatives platforms, and market participants, and which specific risks or market structures regulators identify as priorities in their review. The timeline to Federal Register publication and the scope of final rules, once issued, will signal how aggressively the CFTC intends to extend derivatives oversight into compute markets.
body: The CFTC announced a 60-day comment period on derivatives contracts for compute commodities, seeking public input on how federal regulators should oversee trading in what officials frame as the foundational asset of the AI economy. The request covers cash market size and liquidity, market oversight and manipulation concerns, customer protection standards, and the treatment of perpetual compute futures.

According to the CFTC's announcement, Chairman Michael S. Selig stated that "America cannot win the AI race without a robust derivatives market for compute," and described the request as "the first step toward establishing clear rules of the road for American compute markets." The agency positioned compute alongside historical commodity markets, with Selig noting that "just as American markets helped establish the gold standard for trading the commodities that powered the industrial economy, we will do the same for the commodity that will power the intelligence economy."

The request seeks comment on five specific dimensions: the size and liquidity of underlying compute cash markets, oversight mechanisms and manipulation safeguards, protections for derivatives customers, the structure and risks of perpetual futures contracts in compute, and other considerations the agency deems relevant to establishing a regulatory framework.
Comments will be accepted for 60 days following publication in the Federal Register, per the CFTC's announcement.
